slides.headline: He led a tribal uprising against colonial exploitation. India now marks his birthday as a national day of pride.
Birsa Munda was born on November 15, 1875, in Ulihatu village, present-day Jharkhand.
slides.body: He led the Ulgulan - the "Great Tumult" - a tribal uprising between 1899 and 1900 against British colonial exploitation and the exploitative land practices imposed on tribal communities.

slides.headline: His movement directly led to a law that still protects tribal land today.
slides.body: The uprising forced the colonial government to pass the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act of 1908, protecting tribal land rights. In 2021, the Indian government instituted his birthday as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas - Tribal Pride Day - honoring tribal freedom fighters nationwide.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat has to remember the fights that protected the people furthest from power.
slides.body: Birsa Munda didn't just resist colonial rule - he won a legal protection for tribal land that has outlasted him by more than a century.

sources.text: PIB (Ministry of Tribal Affairs) - Janjatiya Gaurav Divas
